findings.title: totalPages off-by-one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit (e.g. 100 members with limit 50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2, so the 'next' arrow stays enabled and the admin can page past the last page, and the page indicator shows an impossible page count. It should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (and be 0 when there are no members).

findings.title: Remove link shown for members of automatic groups
findings.body: The template guards the remove link with {{#unless automatic}}, but inside the item view the context is the member (a Discourse.User), not the group, so `automatic` is undefined and the link is rendered for automatic groups too. Clicking it fires removeMember, which hits DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members and is rejected with 422 ('can not modify automatic'), leaving the admin with a broken control. The group's automatic flag needs to be passed into the item view (e.g. via a controller or view property).

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group test uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but the remove_member route is DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members. A PUT to that URL routes to add_members, which calls params.require(:usernames) and raises ActionController::ParameterMissing (500/400) rather than returning the asserted 422. The test as written cannot pass against the defined routes and does not actually exercise remove_member; it should use xhr :delete.

findings.title: Unbounded limit on public group members endpoint
findings.body: The members action now applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` directly to the query with no upper bound. The old code capped automatic-group listings at 200 members; now any (anonymous, for visible groups) request can pass limit=1000000 and force the server to load and serialize the entire membership. The limit should be clamped to a sane maximum.

findings.title: add_members silently ignores unknown usernames
findings.body: add_members iterates the comma-separated usernames and only adds users found by User.find_by_username; nonexistent usernames are silently skipped and success_json is still returned. The admin UI gives no feedback that some members were not added (previous PATCH-based code had tests asserting this behavior; those tests were deleted rather than ported). Either report which usernames could not be added, or fail the request.

findings.title: Save error handler assumes JSON response body
findings.body: On failure the save action does $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors. If the server returns a non-JSON error (e.g. 500 HTML page, or a response handled by Discourse's global error handling that returns no body), parseJSON throws and the user sees no message, and 'disableSave' is still reset only because the throw happens inside .then's callback which still triggers .finally — but bootbox.alert is never called. Guard the parse or use a fallback message.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined for unnamed groups, breaking promise chains
findings.body: When the group has no name, findMembers now returns undefined instead of a resolved promise (the old code returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([])). Any caller that chains .then on the result (e.g. future code in routes that return model.findMembers() from setupController/model hooks) will crash on undefined. Return RSVP.resolve() to keep the contract.
